_comment: Copy to core.json and replace both secrets before running. core.json is gitignored so real secrets never reach the repository. scripts/setup-kali.sh --secrets-only generates one for you.
_admin: The key to the room. The controller and the MCP server hold it. Never handed to a teammate.
_join: Baked into the script Core serves at /join. Any device that presents it enrolls and is assigned the next free number. A leaked join secret only lets someone put JARVIS on their own screen; controlling other machines still needs the admin token.
_wifi: Recorded so the setup script and the operator agree on one passphrase. Core never uses these to authenticate anything.
_voice: How JARVIS sounds. See scripts/warm-voice.sh — pre-generating the scripted lines is what makes a cloud voice safe to use live.

voice._comment: How JARVIS sounds. provider 'auto' picks the most natural thing installed: gemini, then piper, then the platform's built-in. Cached lines need neither.
voice._style: Prepended to every line sent to Gemini. This is what makes delivery measured rather than chirpy — it is the single biggest lever on how JARVIS sounds.
voice.style: Speak calmly and with dry composure, in a refined British accent, unhurried and understated

gemini._comment: Free tier. Get a key at aistudio.google.com. GEMINI_API_KEY in the environment works too and keeps it out of this file.
gemini._voice: Charon is informative and measured. Kore is firmer. 30 to choose from.

piper._comment: Local neural voice, no internet. pip install piper-tts, then download an en_GB onnx model and point this at it.
